description: Check the citations of YOUR OWN answer against the cited source chunks — Matrix' citation attribution check for answers about documents, regulations and legal norms. Pass the answer text and `chunk_ids`; mark every claim with [n] = n-th entry (1-based) of chunk_ids, or with [chunk:<id>] (the id is added to the list). Answers without markers are rejected. Also list the retrieved chunks you did NOT cite: they are the candidates a better source is searched among. Per citing statement and marker the verdict is `supported` (verbatim quote found, or the cited/co-cited chunk carries at least 30% of the statement's weighted key terms — a plausibility check, NOT proof that the chunk states the claim), `better_candidate` (another listed chunk carries it — term overlap and embedding similarity agree; see alt_chunk_id), `suspect` (another chunk looks better on term overlap only, or a quoted text is not in the cited chunk; `embedding_issue` says why the embedding check could not run) or `not_judged` (too little content, or weak overlap with no better chunk to compare — NOT a confirmation). A quote that exists only in an AI-generated image description is no source text: its citations have `quote: found_in_generated_description` and are counted under `summary.from_generated_description`, never under `supported`. Each citation reports the cited chunk's context_id and document — check that it is the context you meant — and `page` (`page_end` over a page break): the PDF page a verified quote stands on, otherwise the cited chunk's pages. At most 100 citing statements are judged per call (`truncated` says how many were skipped). Embeddings are only compared within one embedding model.

answer.description: Your answer text with citation markers [n] or [chunk:<id>].

chunk_ids.description: Chunk ids in marker order ([1] = first entry), plus uncited retrieved chunks as candidates. No duplicates. May be omitted when the answer only uses [chunk:<id>] markers.

name: verify_citations
